acceptance: pi_rpc_process.rs implements the algorithm above: a MAX_RECORD_BYTES constant of 16 MiB, `read_stdout_lines` delegating to `pub(super) fn read_stdout_lines_bounded(.., max_bytes: usize)`, and the per-line `take(max_bytes + 1)` bound applied on the READ. Normal behavior (LF/CRLF framing, U+2028 staying inside a record, non-JSON line -> Error, Exited exactly once) is unchanged. The file stays under 600 lines

pi_rpc_process_bound_tests.rs (declared in mod.rs as its own `#[cfg(test)]` line directly followed by `mod pi_rpc_process_bound_tests;`, inserted between existing pairs) tests read_stdout_lines_bounded with `std::io::Cursor<Vec<u8>>` input, an mpsc channel, and a small cap (use 16): (1) two short valid JSON lines -> two Record values then Exited; (2) one line of 40 content bytes between two short valid lines -> Record, exactly one Error whose text contains "exceeds", Record (the later line is still parsed), Exited; (3) a valid JSON line whose content is EXACTLY 16 bytes (e.g. {"a":"1234567"} padded to 16) followed by LF is a Record, and the same with 17 content bytes is an Error; (4) a final over-long line with NO trailing LF at EOF -> one Error then Exited (and no Record); (5) two consecutive over-long lines -> two Errors; (6) CRLF-terminated short line still parses; (7) a 3-byte-per-char string containing U+2028 inside a valid JSON line shorter than the cap is still ONE record
The existing tests in pi_rpc_process_tests.rs and everywhere else are NOT edited and still pass; no other source file is edited; production behavior elsewhere is unchanged
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo nextest run --workspace` pass (0 failures); the new bound tests are LISTED in the nextest output
user_request: Security review finding on commit a70105d4: bound the line length in the Pi/sidecar JSONL stdout reader (resource bound placed on the read, not after the buffer has grown).
